title: Binance now lets AI agents trade, but keeping them in check is largely up to users
slides: Can AI agents be trusted with your crypto?
Binance now lets them trade autonomously.
But Binance says users must monitor everything.

thread_text:
1. Your crypto, their control?

Binance now lets AI agents trade autonomously. But they're not accountable if it goes wrong.

2. The fine print

Binance says users must monitor everything. No exceptions.

3. Set limits or lose

You must set strict limits on every trade. Without them, the AI has no guardrails.

4. Start small

Before trusting AI, test with tiny amounts. This is the only safe way to learn its behavior.

5. Are you ready?

Will you hand over your wallet to an AI this week? If yes, start with $10 and watch closely.

script: Can AI agents be trusted with your crypto?
Binance now lets them trade autonomously.
Set limits and watch every trade.

instagram.caption:
Your crypto can now be moved by an AI agent on Binance, no human click required. 🕹️

The exchange rolled out autonomous trading for AI agents, but the fine print is blunt: you’re the babysitter. Binance explicitly says users must monitor every single trade and set their own limits—if the bot goes rogue, that’s on you, not them.

For anyone running a trading bot or letting an agent manage a wallet, the workflow just changed: you now need hard caps on position size and a kill switch, or the AI has zero guardrails. 🚦

Before you trust one with real money, run it on $10 and watch every move for a week. Would you hand over your keys to a bot this Friday, or is that a hard no? 💸
